notes.meaning: Paul explains that serving God in the new covenant is a great honor given purely by God's mercy. Because of that mercy, he and his fellow workers do not lose courage or give up when difficulties arise. They trust that the God who called them will help them all the way to the end.

Paul refuses to use shameful secrets, clever tricks, or watered-down teaching to win people over. Instead, he speaks God's truth plainly and openly for everyone to hear. He leaves the message to each person's conscience, knowing that God is watching everything he does.

If some people cannot see the truth of the gospel, the problem is not that the message is unclear. The good news shines brightly, just like the sun in the sky. It remains hidden only to those who are on the path to ruin because they reject it.

Satan rules over this sinful world and actively blinds the minds of unbelievers. He keeps them in spiritual darkness so they cannot see the radiant glory of Christ, who shows us exactly what God is like. Unbelievers freely choose to ignore the truth, and Satan strengthens their blindness.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Several early church leaders, including Augustine and Chrysostom, read this to mean the true God judicially blinds those who stubbornly refuse to believe.

notes.meaning: The apostles do not preach to make themselves popular, rich, or powerful. Their whole message focuses on Jesus Christ as the true Lord and ruler of all. In relation to other believers, they see themselves simply as servants who help others for Jesus' sake.

At the beginning of creation, God commanded physical light to shine into the darkness with a single word. In the same powerful way, God shines into human hearts to drive away spiritual darkness. Through this inner light, believers come to know God's true character and glory seen in the person of Jesus Christ.

The priceless treasure of the gospel is placed inside fragile human beings who are like cheap clay jars. God planned it this way so that no one could claim the results came from human greatness. The surpassing power to change lives belongs entirely to God, not to His workers.

Paul describes the hardships of his ministry using four sharp contrasts. Hard times pressed him on all sides, puzzled him, chased him down, and knocked him flat, but God never abandoned him. Though his human body was battered, God's power kept him from being crushed or destroyed.

Serving Jesus brought daily danger and suffering that mirrored the death of Christ. Yet being preserved through these constant perils proved that Jesus' living power was real in their fragile bodies. Their bodily trials showed the dying of Jesus, while their daily survival showed His resurrection life.

Paul and his companions faced constant danger and exhaustion so that others could hear the good news. While death was constantly threatening the apostles, the believers in Corinth were enjoying new spiritual life and peace. The ministers willingly bore the cost of suffering so the church could thrive.

Paul quotes Psalm 116 to show that genuine faith naturally leads to bold speech. Just as the ancient psalmist trusted God during deep trouble and spoke out, the apostles preach because they truly believe God's message. Strong faith in the heart gives believers the courage to speak the truth.

differ.view: Believers understand this as faith produced by the Holy Spirit, who plants trust in the hearts of God's people.
Believers see this as sharing the same trusting disposition and frame of heart that moved ancient saints like David to speak.

notes.meaning: Paul faced death without fear because he knew that God raised the Lord Jesus from the grave. That same power guarantees that all believers will be raised to life at the final day. God will gather ministers and their converts together to stand joyfully in His presence.

Everything the apostles suffered was done for the benefit of the church. As more people received God's grace and forgiveness, a larger circle of voices gave Him thanks. When many people praise God for saving them, God receives greater honor.

Hardship and aging slowly wear down the physical body, but believers do not give up in despair. God supplies fresh spiritual strength and courage to the inner soul every single day. Physical decay cannot stop the spiritual growth that prepares a believer for heaven.

Present sufferings may feel heavy, but compared to eternity they are brief and lightweight. God uses these temporary trials to prepare believers for an everlasting glory of immense worth. Knowing that future joy far outweighs present pain gives Christians strength to endure.

Believers do not focus their main attention on visible things like wealth, comfort, or present troubles, which will all pass away. Instead, they fix their eyes on unseen realities like God, Christ, and the eternal life ahead. Keeping an eye on what lasts forever keeps daily trials in their proper place.
